title: Kong Gateway adds FIPS 140-3 support for regulated deployments
summary: Kong Gateway now ships separate FIPS 140-3 artifacts alongside its existing FIPS 140-2 builds, reducing compliance and migration friction for federal, financial-services, healthcare, and other regulated deployments. This expands commercial eligibility and protects regulated-customer retention, but does not change the thesis score because Kong disclosed no related customer wins, contracts, bookings, ARR, or revenue contribution.
confirmed: Kong announced that Gateway supports FIPS 140-3 through separately named packages and container images published alongside existing FIPS 140-2 artifacts.

Kong says the FIPS 140-3 build uses OpenSSL FIPS provider 3.1.2, adds TLS 1.3 in FIPS mode, narrows the default TLS 1.2 cipher suite, and centralizes cryptographic policy across runtime and signing paths.
Existing FIPS 140-2 deployments can remain on their current artifacts, while customers can opt into the FIPS 140-3 build without re-architecting their Kong Gateway deployment.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose the number or value of customers requiring FIPS 140-3, any related federal or regulated-industry contract, pricing, bookings, ARR, retention effect, or revenue contribution.

The announcement describes Kong's use of a validated OpenSSL FIPS provider; it does not establish that every Kong deployment, surrounding system, or customer compliance program is independently certified merely by installing the artifact.
